records.issue_text: **Test coverage** — `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each contain exactly one test: asserting the controller is a subclass of `AdminController`. None of `create`/`update`/`destroy`, the `category_id` defaulting-to-uncategorized behavior, validation-failure responses, or the `embedding#show` payload shape are exercised. This is the entire new CRUD surface that is the point of the PR, and it's effectively untested; nothing added covers the JS component/route/controller either.
records.rationale: The diff adds new controllers with nontrivial behavior (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy with category_id defaulting and save error handling; Admin::EmbeddingController#show/update payload with embeddable_hosts), but the new specs `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each only assert inheritance

records.issue_text: **`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2`** — The format regex requires a dotted hostname with a 2–5 letter alphabetic TLD, rejecting legitimate values like `localhost:3000`, bare IPs, or longer modern TLDs (`.london`, `.company`). Combined with the migration's raw INSERT bypassing this same validation, any pre-existing host of that shape becomes permanently un-editable/un-resavable through the new admin UI (validation blocks it, but it was never cleaned on insert either).
records.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost` with `validates_format_of :host` using `/\A...\.[a-z]{2,5}...\Z/i` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2), which indeed rejects hosts without a dot (e.g. `localhost`) and TLDs longer than 5 chars (e.g. `.london`). The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` populates `embeddable_hosts` via raw `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` without running mod

records.rationale: In `store.js.es6`, the new plural-IDs branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `.map()` always returns an Array (truthy even if empty), the `|| []` fallback is effectively unreachable here.
